coboundary subgroup.**

The point of stating this with the chart indices `s`, `t` as **variables** constrained by

/-- **(iii-a): the two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹` of units maps to the Picard group.** The comparison
homomorphism

```
Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ (im Γ(V₀)ˣ · im Γ(V₁)ˣ)  →*  X.CechPic
```

descended from `twoChartClassHom` along `twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff`. The source is exactly
the carrier the truncated-exponential engine of `Tangent/TruncExpCech.lean` computes, so this
is the arrow joining the (landed) T2 engine to the definitional Picard group. -/
noncomputable def twoChartClass (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel) :
    (Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ ⧸ TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
        (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))) →* X.CechPic :=
  QuotientGroup.lift _ (twoChartClassHom V sel hmem) fun u hu =>
    (twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff V sel hmem hsel u).mpr hu

@[simp]
theorem twoChartClass_mk (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
    (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) :
    twoChartClass V sel hmem hsel (QuotientGroup.mk u) = twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u :=
  rfl

exactly when its representative is a coboundary, i.e. when it was already trivial. The
mathematical content is the landed refinement injectivity, which is what makes the `→`
half of that iff true. -/
theorem twoChartClass_injective (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel) :
    Function.Injective (twoChartClass V sel hmem hsel) := by

  | H u =>
    rw [twoChartClass_mk, twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff V sel hmem hsel u,

end Scheme

lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :
    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C T').comap (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) := by
  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨CechPic.map g.left N, ?_⟩
  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)
      = CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
    ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whiskerLeft_snd]

/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along `g : T' ⟶ T`: pull back along
`C ◁ g` and descend to the quotients. -/
noncomputable def relPicMap (g : T' ⟶ T) : relPic C T →* relPic C T' :=
  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C T')
    (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) (picFromBase_le_comap C g)

@[simp]
lemma relPicMap_mk (g : T' ⟶ T) (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
    relPicMap C g (relPicMk C T L) = relPicMk C T' (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left L) :=
  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L

lemma relPicMap_id (x : relPic C T) : relPicMap C (𝟙 T) x = x := by
  induction x using relPic.ind with
  | mk L =>
    rw [relPicMap_mk, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id, Over.id_left,
      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
    rfl

lemma relPicMap_comp (g : T' ⟶ T) (h : T'' ⟶ T') (x : relPic C T) :
    relPicMap C (h ≫ g) x = relPicMap C h (relPicMap C g x) := by
  induction x using relPic.ind with
  | mk L =>
    rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk]
    refine congrArg (relPicMk C T'') ?_
    rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
      ← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp]

/-- The relative Picard functor `T ↦ Pic(C ⊗ T)/Pic(T)` of Grothendieck–Kleiman, as a

---
name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

/-! ## The compatibility square (what makes the reduction usable, not merely true) -/

/-- **The equivalence intertwines restriction along `g` with pullback of Čech classes.**

Without this, `relPicMulEquivCechPic` would identify the two *groups* at each end of the
`ε`-restriction while saying nothing about the *map* between them — and it is the kernel of
that map that Wave 5 computes. With it, the statement
`ker(relPic(k[ε]) → relPic(k)) ≃ ker(CechPic(C_ε) → CechPic(C))` is immediate.

The proof is `relPicMap_mk`: the relative restriction is *defined* as `CechPic.map (C ◁ g)`
descended to the quotients, so once the quotient is trivial there is nothing left to check.
Recorded explicitly because "the groups agree" and "the maps agree" are different claims and
only the second one is usable. -/
theorem relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMap (T T' : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [Subsingleton T.left] [Subsingleton T'.left] (g : T' ⟶ T) (x : relPic C T) :
    relPicMulEquivCechPic C T' (relPicMap C g x)
      = Scheme.CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (relPicMulEquivCechPic C T x) := by
  induction x using relPic.ind with
  | mk L => rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMk, relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMk]

end AlgebraicGeometry

10	/-!
11	# The two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹` of units embeds in the Picard group (W5-T4 clause (iii-a)/(iii-b))
12	
13	For a scheme `X` with two opens `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, the two-chart Čech cohomology of units
14	
15	```
16	Ȟ¹(V₀,V₁ ; 𝒪ˣ)  =  Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ (im Γ(V₀)ˣ · im Γ(V₁)ˣ)
17	```
18	
19	maps to the definitional Picard group `X.CechPic`, **injectively**
20	(`Scheme.twoChartClass_injective`). This file builds that map and proves the injectivity.
21	
22	## Why this file exists: clauses (iii-a) and (iii-b), which are not about dual numbers
23	
24	`informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §6 splits the Wave-5 residue "clause (iii)" — the last input to
25	the Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11 dimension identity — into three parts, and observes that **two of
26	them contain no dual numbers, no curves and no `H¹`**. Those two are exactly this file:
27	
28	* **(iii-a)** the comparison homomorphism `twoChartClass` exists;
29	* **(iii-b)** it is injective.
30	
31	Both are general statements about a scheme with a two-open cover, so they are stated here at
32	that generality rather than at `C ×_k Spec k[ε]`. The remaining part, **(iii-c)**
33	(surjectivity onto the `ε`-kernel), is the only one that needs the thickening; it consumes
34	`DualNumber.free_of_cyclic_mod_eps` and lives elsewhere.
35	
36	The two-chart Čech quotient here is the **same carrier** the truncated-exponential engine of
37	`Tangent/TruncExpCech.lean` computes: `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits` of the two restriction
38	maps. So `twoChartClass` is precisely the arrow that connects the (landed) T2 engine to the
39	(definitional) Picard group, in the direction the tangent computation needs.
40	
41	## Implementation notes
42	
43	`CechPic` is built on **pointed** covers — one open per point — so a two-open cover enters
44	through a selector `sel : X → Bool` with `x ∈ V (sel x)`, exactly as
45	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.pieceIndex` and `thetaFieldChartIndex` do elsewhere in the tree.
46	Indexing the charts by `Bool` (rather than by two named opens) is what makes the cocycle law a
47	`cases`-bash that closes uniformly.
48	
49	The cocycle attached to an overlap unit `u` has pair values `1` on the diagonal, `u` at
50	`(0,1)` and the `inf_comm`-transport of `u⁻¹` at `(1,0)` (`Scheme.twoChartPairUnit`).
51	
52	**A negative result, recorded so it is not retried** (worksheet §6.2): the slick spelling
53	`pairUnit s t = u ^ (δ t − δ s)`, which would close the cocycle law by `zpow_add` alone, does
54	**not** typecheck. On the diagonal the ambient open `T` need only be `≤ V s`, where `u` — a
55	section on `V₀ ⊓ V₁` — cannot be restricted at all. The exponent trick needs a unit on the
56	union and there is none. The eight-case `cases` bash is the honest route, and it is three
57	lines.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60	
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartPairUnit` — the pair values, with
62	  `twoChartPairUnit_trans` (the cocycle law, all eight `Bool` cases) and
63	  `twoChartPairUnit_mul` (multiplicativity in the overlap unit).
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartCover` — the pointed cover of a selector.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartCocycle` — the unit Čech 1-cocycle of an overlap unit.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartClassHom` — `Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ →* X.CechPic`, the map before
67	  passing to the quotient, with `twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff` (the kernel computation, where
68	  refinement injectivity enters).
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartClass` — **(iii-a)**: the induced homomorphism
70	  `Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits → X.CechPic`.
71	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartClass_injective` — **(iii-b)**.
72	
73	## What the surjectivity hypothesis is for
74	
75	`twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff` and everything downstream take `hsel : Function.Surjective sel`
76	— the selector must actually use both charts. This is not bookkeeping: the cobounding
77	`0`-cochain produced by refinement injectivity is indexed by *points*, and turning it into a
78	pair of *chart* units needs one point assigned to each chart. See that lemma's docstring.
79	
80	A second trap recorded at `twoChartCoboundary_of_pairRelation`: transporting a chart unit
81	along `sel i = false` with `▸` produces an ill-typed motive, because the type of a section
82	depends on the open which depends on the `Bool`. Abstracting the chart indices as variables
83	and using `subst` avoids the transport entirely.
84	
85	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5, proof of Thm. 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020).
86	-/

100	/-- `Units.map` of the section-restriction ring map **is** `unitsRestrict`, definitionally.
101	Named so that the two spellings — the one `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits` is stated in and
102	the one the Čech cocycle API uses — can be rewritten into each other. -/
103	@[simp]
104	theorem unitsMap_resHom {U W : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U) :
105	    Units.map (X.resHom h).toMonoidHom = X.unitsRestrict h :=
106	  rfl
107	
108	/-! ## The pair values of an overlap unit -/
109	
110	/-- **The pair values of the two-chart cocycle attached to an overlap unit `u`.** Trivial on
111	the diagonal, `u` at `(0,1)`, and the `inf_comm`-transport of `u⁻¹` at `(1,0)`.
112	
113	The diagonal entries are forced to be `1`: a cocycle value at `(s,s)` lives on opens contained
114	in `V s` alone, where an overlap section has no meaning. This is also why the `zpow` spelling
115	of these values does not typecheck — see the module docstring. -/
116	noncomputable def twoChartPairUnit (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) :
117	    ∀ s t : Bool, Γ(X, V s ⊓ V t)ˣ
118	  | false, false => 1
119	  | true,  true  => 1
120	  | false, true  => u
121	  | true,  false => X.unitsRestrict (le_of_eq (inf_comm _ _)) u⁻¹
122	
123	/-- **The cocycle law for the two-chart pair values**, in the form
124	`PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs` consumes: on any open `T` below the three relevant
125	overlaps, the product of the `(s,t)` and `(t,r)` values is the `(s,r)` value.
126	
127	All eight `Bool` cases at once: the four with `s = r` cancel `u · u⁻¹`, the four others are
128	`1 · u = u` after the diagonal entries reduce. -/
129	theorem twoChartPairUnit_trans (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) (s t r : Bool) (T : X.Opens)
130	    (h₀ : T ≤ V s ⊓ V t) (h₁ : T ≤ V t ⊓ V r) (h₂ : T ≤ V s ⊓ V r) :
131	    X.unitsRestrict h₀ (twoChartPairUnit u s t)
132	        * X.unitsRestrict h₁ (twoChartPairUnit u t r)
133	      = X.unitsRestrict h₂ (twoChartPairUnit u s r) := by
134	  cases s <;> cases t <;> cases r <;>
135	    simp only [twoChartPairUnit, map_one, one_mul, mul_one, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict,
136	      map_inv] <;>
137	    first | rfl | exact mul_inv_cancel _
138	
139	/-- The pair values are multiplicative in the overlap unit — the input to
140	`twoChartClassHom` being a group homomorphism. -/
141	theorem twoChartPairUnit_mul (u v : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) (s t : Bool) :
142	    twoChartPairUnit (u * v) s t = twoChartPairUnit u s t * twoChartPairUnit v s t := by
143	  cases s <;> cases t <;>
144	    (simp only [twoChartPairUnit, mul_one, mul_inv_rev, map_mul, map_inv]
145	     try first | rfl | exact mul_comm _ _)
146	
147	/-- The pair values of the unit `1` are trivial. -/
148	@[simp]
149	theorem twoChartPairUnit_one (s t : Bool) :
150	    twoChartPairUnit (V := V) 1 s t = 1 := by
151	  cases s <;> cases t <;> simp [twoChartPairUnit]
152	
153	/-! ## The pointed cover of a selector -/
154	
155	/-- **The pointed cover attached to a chart selector.** A two-open cover becomes a pointed
156	cover (one open per point) by choosing, for each `x`, a chart containing it — the same pattern
157	as `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.pieceIndex` and `thetaFieldChartIndex`. -/
158	noncomputable def twoChartCover (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
159	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) : X.PointedCover where
160	  opens x := V (sel x)
161	  mem_opens := hmem
162	
163	@[simp]
164	theorem twoChartCover_opens (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
165	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (x : X) :
166	    (twoChartCover V sel hmem).opens x = V (sel x) :=
167	  rfl
168	
169	/-- The pair value of the two-chart cocycle at a pair of points, retyped on the overlap of
170	the pointed cover's members. -/
171	noncomputable def twoChartCoverUnit (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) (sel : X → Bool)
172	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (x y : X) :
173	    Γ(X, (twoChartCover V sel hmem).opens x ⊓ (twoChartCover V sel hmem).opens y)ˣ :=
174	  twoChartPairUnit u (sel x) (sel y)
175	
176	/-- **The unit Čech 1-cocycle of an overlap unit** on the two-chart pointed cover. -/
177	noncomputable def twoChartCocycle (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) (sel : X → Bool)
178	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) : X.unitsCocycle (twoChartCover V sel hmem) :=
179	  OneCocycle.ofPairs (G := X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
180	    (U := (twoChartCover V sel hmem).opens)
181	    (fun x y => twoChartCoverUnit u sel hmem x y)
182	    (fun x y z => twoChartPairUnit_trans u (sel x) (sel y) (sel z) _ _ _ _)

184	@[simp]
185	theorem twoChartCocycle_unitsEvInf (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) (sel : X → Bool)
186	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (x y : X) :
187	    Scheme.unitsEvInf (twoChartCocycle u sel hmem) x y = twoChartPairUnit u (sel x) (sel y) :=
188	  OneCocycle.ofPairs_evInf (G := X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
189	    (U := (twoChartCover V sel hmem).opens) _ _ x y

191	/-- Cocycles are determined by their pair values (`unitsEvInf`), so a two-chart cocycle
192	identity can be checked pointwise on pairs. -/
193	theorem twoChartCocycle_eq_iff (u v : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) (sel : X → Bool)
194	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) :
195	    twoChartCocycle u sel hmem = twoChartCocycle v sel hmem
196	      ↔ ∀ x y : X, twoChartPairUnit u (sel x) (sel y) = twoChartPairUnit v (sel x) (sel y) := by
197	  constructor
198	  · intro h x y
199	    have h' := congrArg (fun γ => Scheme.unitsEvInf γ x y) h
200	    rw [twoChartCocycle_unitsEvInf, twoChartCocycle_unitsEvInf] at h'
201	    exact h'
202	  · intro h
203	    refine OneCocycle.ext (OneCochain.ext ?_)
204	    funext i j T a b
205	    change Scheme.unitsRestrict X _ (twoChartPairUnit u (sel i) (sel j))
206	      = Scheme.unitsRestrict X _ (twoChartPairUnit v (sel i) (sel j))
207	    rw [h i j]

209	/-- The two-chart cocycle of the unit `1` is trivial. -/
210	@[simp]
211	theorem twoChartCocycle_one (sel : X → Bool) (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) :
212	    twoChartCocycle (V := V) 1 sel hmem = 1 := by
213	  refine OneCocycle.ext (OneCochain.ext ?_)
214	  funext i j T a b
215	  change Scheme.unitsRestrict X _ (twoChartPairUnit (V := V) 1 (sel i) (sel j)) = 1
216	  rw [twoChartPairUnit_one, map_one]

219	theorem twoChartCocycle_mul (u v : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) (sel : X → Bool)
220	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) :
221	    twoChartCocycle (u * v) sel hmem = twoChartCocycle u sel hmem * twoChartCocycle v sel hmem := by
222	  refine OneCocycle.ext (OneCochain.ext ?_)
223	  funext i j T a b
224	  change Scheme.unitsRestrict X _ (twoChartPairUnit (u * v) (sel i) (sel j))
225	    = Scheme.unitsRestrict X _ (twoChartPairUnit u (sel i) (sel j))
226	      * Scheme.unitsRestrict X _ (twoChartPairUnit v (sel i) (sel j))
227	  rw [twoChartPairUnit_mul, map_mul]
228	  rfl

230	/-! ## The comparison homomorphism into the Picard group -/
231	
232	/-- **The Čech Picard class of an overlap unit**, on the two-chart pointed cover: a group
233	homomorphism `Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ →* X.CechPic`. This is (iii-a) before passing to the quotient by
234	the coboundaries. -/
235	noncomputable def twoChartClassHom (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
236	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ →* X.CechPic where
237	  toFun u := Scheme.CechPic.mk (twoChartCover V sel hmem) (twoChartCocycle u sel hmem).class
238	  map_one' := by rw [twoChartCocycle_one]; exact Scheme.CechPic.mk_one _
239	  map_mul' u v := by
240	    rw [Scheme.CechPic.mk_mul_mk, twoChartCocycle_mul]
241	    rfl
242	
243	@[simp]
244	theorem twoChartClassHom_apply (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
245	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) :
246	    twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u
247	      = Scheme.CechPic.mk (twoChartCover V sel hmem) (twoChartCocycle u sel hmem).class :=
248	  rfl

250	/-! ## (iii-b): the kernel of the comparison is exactly the coboundaries -/
251	
252	/-- **The `0`-cochain exhibiting a coboundary unit as a coboundary.** For chart units
253	`v₁ ∈ Γ(V₀)ˣ`, `v₂ ∈ Γ(V₁)ˣ`, the family `false ↦ v₁⁻¹`, `true ↦ v₂`.
254	
255	Written as a dependent match on the `Bool` so that each branch has the *right type on the
256	nose* — no transport along an equality of opens is needed anywhere, which is the whole reason
257	the charts are indexed by `Bool` in this file. -/
258	noncomputable def twoChartCob (v₁ : Γ(X, V false)ˣ) (v₂ : Γ(X, V true)ˣ) :
259	    ∀ s : Bool, Γ(X, V s)ˣ
260	  | false => v₁⁻¹
261	  | true  => v₂
262	
263	/-- **The coboundary relation for `twoChartCob`**: if `u = ρ₀(v₁) · ρ₁(v₂)` then the
264	`0`-cochain `twoChartCob v₁ v₂` conjugates the pair values of `u` to `1`. All four `Bool`
265	cases; the two off-diagonal ones are where the hypothesis is spent. -/
266	theorem twoChartCob_spec (v₁ : Γ(X, V false)ˣ) (v₂ : Γ(X, V true)ˣ)
267	    (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ)
268	    (hv : Units.map (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false)).toMonoidHom v₁
269	        * Units.map (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true)).toMonoidHom v₂ = u)
270	    (s t : Bool) (T : X.Opens) (h₀ : T ≤ V s ⊓ V t) (ha : T ≤ V s) (hb : T ≤ V t) :
271	    X.unitsRestrict ha (twoChartCob v₁ v₂ s) * X.unitsRestrict h₀ (twoChartPairUnit u s t)
272	      = X.unitsRestrict hb (twoChartCob v₁ v₂ t) := by
273	  subst hv
274	  cases s <;> cases t <;>
275	    (simp only [twoChartCob, twoChartPairUnit, map_one, mul_one, map_mul, map_inv,
276	       unitsMap_resHom, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict]
277	     try first | rfl | (rw [inv_mul_cancel_left]) | group)
278	
279	/-- **From a coboundary relation at a mixed pair of chart indices to membership in the
280	coboundary subgroup.**
281	
282	The point of stating this with the chart indices `s`, `t` as **variables** constrained by
283	`hs : s = false`, `ht : t = true` — rather than substituting `false`/`true` directly — is that
284	the two chart units arrive as `α i : Γ(V (sel i))ˣ` for points `i`, and `sel i = false` is a
285	*propositional* equality. Rewriting the goal along it with `▸` produces an ill-typed motive
286	(the section type depends on the open, which depends on the Bool). With the indices abstract,
287	`subst` does the same work with no transport at all.
288	
289	Recorded because the `▸` route looks obviously right and fails with a `motive is not type
290	correct` error that reads as though the statement were wrong. -/
291	theorem twoChartCoboundary_of_pairRelation {s t : Bool} (hs : s = false) (ht : t = true)
292	    (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) (a : Γ(X, V s)ˣ) (b : Γ(X, V t)ˣ)
293	    (key : X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : V s ⊓ V t ≤ V s) a * twoChartPairUnit u s t
294	      = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right b) :
295	    u ∈ TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
296	      (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
297	      (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true)) := by
298	  subst hs
299	  subst ht
300	  refine TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mpr ⟨a⁻¹, b, ?_⟩
301	  simp only [unitsMap_resHom, map_inv]
302	  rw [twoChartPairUnit] at key
303	  rw [← key]
304	  group
305	
306	/-- **The Picard class of an overlap unit is trivial iff the unit is a Čech coboundary**
307	— (iii-b), and the heart of this file.
308	
309	`←` is the coboundary computation. `→` is where **refinement injectivity** enters: by the
310	landed `CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff` a Picard class on a fixed cover is trivial only if its `H¹`
311	class already is, so the cobounding `0`-cochain `α : ∀ x, Γ(V (sel x))ˣ` exists *on the
312	two-chart cover itself*. Evaluating the coboundary relation at one point of each chart turns
313	`α` into a pair of chart units exhibiting `u` as a coboundary.
314	
315	**The hypothesis `Function.Surjective sel` is genuinely needed, and is not bookkeeping.** The
316	`0`-cochain `α` is indexed by *points*; to extract the two chart units the argument needs a
317	point assigned to each chart. If `sel` misses a value, the cover is really a one-chart cover
318	and no chart unit for the missing chart is produced. (Note the missing-chart case is not a
319	counterexample to the statement — if `V false = ⊥` then `Γ(V false ⊓ V true)ˣ` is trivial
320	anyway — but it is not *provable* along this route, so the hypothesis stays.) -/
321	theorem twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
322	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
323	    (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) :
324	    twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u = 1
325	      ↔ u ∈ TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
326	          (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
327	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true)) := by
328	  constructor
329	  · intro h
330	    -- refinement injectivity: the `H¹` class is already trivial on the two-chart cover
331	    rw [twoChartClassHom_apply, Scheme.CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff,
332	      show (1 : X.unitsH1 (twoChartCover V sel hmem)) = OneCocycle.class 1 from rfl] at h
333	    obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ :=
334	      (OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mp ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp h)
335	    -- pick a point in each chart
336	    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hsel false
337	    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hsel true
338	    have key : X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : V (sel i) ⊓ V (sel j) ≤ V (sel i)) (α i)
339	        * twoChartPairUnit u (sel i) (sel j)
340	          = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (α j) := by
341	      have h1 := hα i j
342	      rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul] at h1
343	      rw [← twoChartCocycle_unitsEvInf u sel hmem i j]
344	      exact h1
345	    exact twoChartCoboundary_of_pairRelation hi hj u (α i) (α j) key
346	  · intro h
347	    obtain ⟨v₁, v₂, hv⟩ := TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp h
348	    rw [twoChartClassHom_apply,
349	      show (1 : X.CechPic) = Scheme.CechPic.mk (twoChartCover V sel hmem) 1 from
350	        (Scheme.CechPic.mk_one _).symm]
351	    refine congrArg _ ?_
352	    rw [show (1 : X.unitsH1 (twoChartCover V sel hmem)) = OneCocycle.class 1 from rfl]
353	    refine (OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mpr
354	      ((OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mpr
355	        ⟨fun x => twoChartCob v₁ v₂ (sel x), fun x y => ?_⟩)
356	    rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul]
357	    exact twoChartCob_spec v₁ v₂ u hv (sel x) (sel y) _ _ _ _
358	
359	/-! ## (iii-a) packaged: the comparison on the two-chart Čech quotient -/
360	
361	/-- **(iii-a): the two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹` of units maps to the Picard group.** The comparison
362	homomorphism
363	
364	```
365	Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ (im Γ(V₀)ˣ · im Γ(V₁)ˣ)  →*  X.CechPic
366	```
367	
368	descended from `twoChartClassHom` along `twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff`. The source is exactly
369	the carrier the truncated-exponential engine of `Tangent/TruncExpCech.lean` computes, so this
370	is the arrow joining the (landed) T2 engine to the definitional Picard group. -/
371	noncomputable def twoChartClass (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
372	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel) :
373	    (Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ ⧸ TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
374	        (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
375	        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))) →* X.CechPic :=
376	  QuotientGroup.lift _ (twoChartClassHom V sel hmem) fun u hu =>
377	    (twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff V sel hmem hsel u).mpr hu
378	
379	@[simp]
380	theorem twoChartClass_mk (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
381	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
382	    (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) :
383	    twoChartClass V sel hmem hsel (QuotientGroup.mk u) = twoChartClassHom V sel hmem u :=
384	  rfl
385	
386	/-- **(iii-b): the comparison is injective** — `Ȟ¹(V₀,V₁ ; 𝒪ˣ) ↪ Pic(X)`.
387	
388	Both halves come from `twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff`: a quotient class dies in `X.CechPic`
389	exactly when its representative is a coboundary, i.e. when it was already trivial. The
390	mathematical content is the landed refinement injectivity, which is what makes the `→`
391	half of that iff true. -/
392	theorem twoChartClass_injective (V : Bool → X.Opens) (sel : X → Bool)
393	    (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ V (sel x)) (hsel : Function.Surjective sel) :
394	    Function.Injective (twoChartClass V sel hmem hsel) := by
395	  refine (injective_iff_map_eq_one' _).mpr fun q => ?_
396	  induction q using QuotientGroup.induction_on with
397	  | H u =>
398	    rw [twoChartClass_mk, twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff V sel hmem hsel u,
399	      QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff]

8	/-!
9	# The definitional Picard group: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf
10	
11	For a scheme `X`, this file defines the Picard group of record of this development:
12	the Čech cohomology `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site, computed on **pointed
13	covers** (one open per point of `X`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle`) and
14	stabilized along the refinement preorder.
15	
16	## Main declarations
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic`: the Picard group `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` as the quotient
19	  of `Σ 𝒰, X.unitsH1 𝒰` by agreement on a common refinement, with its `CommGroup`
20	  structure and the constructor/eliminator API `CechPic.mk`, `CechPic.ind`,
21	  `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff`, `CechPic.mk_unitsRes`, `CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.map`: contravariant functoriality — for
23	  `f : X ⟶ Y` the pullback `Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic` — with the strict functor laws
24	  `CechPic.map_id` and `CechPic.map_comp` (the lane keystone).
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`: on a scheme with a
26	  subsingleton underlying space (e.g. `Spec` of a field) the Picard group is trivial.
27	-/

43	instance cechPicSetoid (X : Scheme.{u}) : Setoid (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) where
44	  r p q := ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1),
45	    unitsRes h₁ p.2 = unitsRes h₂ q.2
46	  iseqv := by
47	    constructor
48	    · exact fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, le_rfl, le_rfl, rfl⟩
49	    · rintro p q ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
50	      exact ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, e.symm⟩
51	    · rintro p q r ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩
52	      refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_left.trans h₁, inf_le_right.trans h₄, ?_⟩
53	      have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
54	      have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
55	      simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
56	      exact e₁'.trans e₂'

58	/-- The definitional Picard group of a scheme: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf,
59	stabilized along refinement of pointed covers. -/
60	def CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
61	  Quotient (cechPicSetoid X)

65	/-- The Picard class of a unit Čech `H¹` class on a pointed cover. -/
66	def mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : X.CechPic :=
67	  ⟦⟨𝒰, a⟩⟧
68	
69	@[elab_as_elim]
70	theorem ind {motive : X.CechPic → Prop}
71	    (mk : ∀ (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰), motive (mk 𝒰 a)) (x : X.CechPic) :
72	    motive x :=
73	  Quotient.ind (fun p ↦ by obtain ⟨𝒰, a⟩ := p; exact mk 𝒰 a) x
74	
75	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} {a : X.unitsH1 𝒰} {b : X.unitsH1 𝒱} :
76	    mk 𝒰 a = mk 𝒱 b ↔
77	      ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒱),
78	        unitsRes h₁ a = unitsRes h₂ b :=
79	  Quotient.eq

81	/-- Two classes agreeing after restriction to a common refinement are equal; in
82	particular `mk` is invariant under restriction. -/
83	@[simp]
84	theorem mk_unitsRes {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
85	    mk 𝒱 (unitsRes h a) = mk 𝒰 a :=
86	  Quotient.sound ⟨𝒱, le_rfl, h, unitsRes_rfl _⟩

88	private def mulSig (p q : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
89	    Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 :=
90	  ⟨p.1 ⊓ q.1, unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2⟩
91	
92	private lemma mulSig_assoc {𝒰 𝒱 𝒳 : X.PointedCover} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) (b : X.unitsH1 𝒱)
93	    (c : X.unitsH1 𝒳) :
94	    mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳)
95	        (unitsRes inf_le_left (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b) *
96	          unitsRes inf_le_right c)
97	      = mk (𝒰 ⊓ (𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳))
98	        (unitsRes inf_le_left a *
99	          unitsRes inf_le_right (unitsRes inf_le_left b * unitsRes inf_le_right c)) := by
100	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳, le_rfl, (inf_assoc 𝒰 𝒱 𝒳).le, ?_⟩
101	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
102	  exact mul_assoc _ _ _
103	
104	private lemma mulSig_compat {p p' q q' : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰}
105	    (hp : p ≈ p') (hq : q ≈ q') : mulSig p q ≈ mulSig p' q' := by
106	  obtain ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ := hp
107	  obtain ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩ := hq
108	  have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
109	  have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
110	  simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
111	  refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_inf h₁ h₃, inf_le_inf h₂ h₄, ?_⟩
112	  show unitsRes (inf_le_inf h₁ h₃) (unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2)
113	      = unitsRes (inf_le_inf h₂ h₄) (unitsRes inf_le_left p'.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q'.2)
114	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes]
115	  rw [e₁', e₂']
116	
117	instance : CommGroup X.CechPic where
118	  mul := Quotient.map₂ mulSig (fun _ _ hp _ _ hq ↦ mulSig_compat hp hq)
119	  one := mk ⊤ 1
120	  inv := Quotient.map (fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, p.2⁻¹⟩) (by
121	    rintro p p' ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
122	    exact ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, by simp only [map_inv, e]⟩)
123	  mul_assoc a b c := by
124	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
125	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
126	    induction c using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒳 c =>

variable (X) [IsAffine X]

/-- **Surjectivity of the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism**: every class of invertible
modules over the global sections arises from a unit Čech cocycle on a trivializing
pointed cover. -/
theorem toPic_surjective : Function.Surjective (toPic X) := by
  intro c
  obtain ⟨F⟩ := TrivializingFamily.nonempty (X := X) (N := c.AsModule)
  obtain ⟨P⟩ := PointedCover.BasicRefinement.nonempty F.cover
  refine ⟨CechPic.mk F.cover (OneCocycle.class F.cocycle), ?_⟩
  rw [toPic_mk F.cover F.cocycle P, F.pic_cocycle P, CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_self]

/-- The Čech–Picard descent homomorphism of an affine scheme is an isomorphism. -/
theorem toPic_bijective : Function.Bijective (toPic X) :=
  ⟨toPic_injective, toPic_surjective X⟩

end CechPic

/-- **The Čech–Picard dictionary** of an affine scheme: the definitional Čech Picard
group on pointed Zariski covers is mathlib's Picard group of invertible modules over
the global sections. -/

    X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤) :=
  MulEquiv.ofBijective (CechPic.toPic X) (CechPic.toPic_bijective X)

lemma cechPicEquivPic_apply (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] (c : X.CechPic) :
    cechPicEquivPic X c = CechPic.toPic X c :=

51	    (X.unitsRestrict h u : Γ(X, W)) = X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op u :=

57	    (u : Γ(X, U)ˣ) :
58	    X.unitsRestrict h₂ (X.unitsRestrict h₁ u) = X.unitsRestrict (h₂.trans h₁) u := by
59	  ext

63	/-- **Separation for unit sections**: two units on `V` agreeing on all members of a cover
64	of `V` are equal. -/
65	theorem unitsRestrict_eq_of_locally_eq {ι : Type*} {V : X.Opens} {W : ι → X.Opens}
66	    (hle : ∀ i, W i ≤ V) (hcover : V ≤ ⨆ i, W i) (s t : Γ(X, V)ˣ)
67	    (h : ∀ i, X.unitsRestrict (hle i) s = X.unitsRestrict (hle i) t) : s = t := by
68	  ext
69	  exact X.sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq' W V (fun i ↦ homOfLE (hle i)) hcover _ _
70	    (fun i ↦ congrArg Units.val (h i))
71	
72	/-- **Gluing for unit sections**: a family of units on the members of a cover of `V`,
73	compatible on pairwise intersections, glues to a unit on `V`. (The value and the inverse
74	glue separately as sections; the products of the glued sections are locally `1`, hence
75	`1` by separation.) -/
76	theorem exists_unitsRestrict_eq {ι : Type*} {V : X.Opens} {W : ι → X.Opens}
77	    (hle : ∀ i, W i ≤ V) (hcover : V ≤ ⨆ i, W i) (u : ∀ i, Γ(X, W i)ˣ)
78	    (hu : ∀ i j, X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : W i ⊓ W j ≤ W i) (u i)
79	        = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right : W i ⊓ W j ≤ W j) (u j)) :
80	    ∃ s : Γ(X, V)ˣ, ∀ i, X.unitsRestrict (hle i) s = u i := by
81	  have hval : TopCat.Presheaf.IsCompatible X.sheaf.1 W (fun i ↦ ((u i : Γ(X, W i)))) :=
82	    fun i j ↦ congrArg Units.val (hu i j)
83	  have hinv : TopCat.Presheaf.IsCompatible X.sheaf.1 W
84	      (fun i ↦ (((u i)⁻¹ : Γ(X, W i)ˣ) : Γ(X, W i))) := by
85	    intro i j
86	    have h : X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : W i ⊓ W j ≤ W i) (u i)⁻¹
87	        = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right : W i ⊓ W j ≤ W j) (u j)⁻¹ := by
88	      rw [map_inv, map_inv, hu i j]
89	    exact congrArg Units.val h
90	  obtain ⟨sv, hsv, -⟩ :=
91	    X.sheaf.existsUnique_gluing' W V (fun i ↦ homOfLE (hle i)) hcover _ hval
92	  obtain ⟨si, hsi, -⟩ :=
93	    X.sheaf.existsUnique_gluing' W V (fun i ↦ homOfLE (hle i)) hcover _ hinv
94	  have hvi : sv * si = 1 := by
95	    apply X.sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq' W V (fun i ↦ homOfLE (hle i)) hcover
96	    intro i
97	    rw [map_mul, hsv, hsi, map_one]
98	    exact Units.mul_inv _
99	  have hiv : si * sv = 1 := by rw [mul_comm]; exact hvi
100	  exact ⟨⟨sv, si, hvi, hiv⟩, fun i ↦ Units.ext (hsv i)⟩

102	/-! ## Refinement injectivity -/
103	
104	/-- The glued coboundary: if the restriction of the cocycle `γ` on `𝒰` to a refinement
105	`𝒲 ≤ 𝒰` is the coboundary of `α`, then the comparison sections `α z ⋅ γ(i,z)⁻¹` on
106	`𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒲 z` glue to units `β i ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰 i)` exhibiting `γ` as a coboundary on `𝒰`. -/
107	private lemma exists_glued_coboundary {𝒰 𝒲 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰)
108	    (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (α : ∀ z, Γ(X, 𝒲.opens z)ˣ)
109	    (hα : ∀ z z',
110	      X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens z ⊓ 𝒲.opens z' ≤ 𝒲.opens z) (α z)
111	          * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (h z) (h z')) (unitsEvInf γ z z')
112	        = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (α z')) :
113	    ∃ β : ∀ i, Γ(X, 𝒰.opens i)ˣ, ∀ i j,
114	      X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ≤ 𝒰.opens i) (β i)
115	          * unitsEvInf γ i j
116	        = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (β j) := by
117	  -- Step 1: for each `i`, glue the comparison sections over the cover
118	  -- `{𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒲 z}_z` of `𝒰 i`.
119	  have key : ∀ i, ∃ βi : Γ(X, 𝒰.opens i)ˣ, ∀ z : X,
120	      X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z ≤ 𝒰.opens i) βi
121	        = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (α z)
122	          * (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf le_rfl (h z)) (unitsEvInf γ i z))⁻¹ := by
123	    intro i
124	    refine exists_unitsRestrict_eq (fun z ↦ inf_le_left)
125	      (fun w hw ↦ Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨w, hw, 𝒲.mem_opens w⟩) _ (fun z z' ↦ ?_)
126	    -- compatibility on `O := (𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒲 z) ⊓ (𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒲 z')`, from the coboundary relation
127	    -- for `α` and the cocycle identity for `γ` at `(i, z, z')`, both restricted to `O`
128	    have e₁ := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict
129	      (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) (inf_le_right.trans inf_le_right) :
130	        (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z) ⊓ (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z')
131	          ≤ 𝒲.opens z ⊓ 𝒲.opens z')) (hα z z')
132	    have e₂ := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict
133	      (le_inf (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left)
134	          ((inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right).trans (h z)))
135	          ((inf_le_right.trans inf_le_right).trans (h z')) :
136	        (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z) ⊓ (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z')
137	          ≤ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens z ⊓ 𝒰.opens z')) (unitsEvInf_trans γ i z z')
138	    simp only [map_mul, map_inv, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e₁ e₂ ⊢
139	    rw [← e₁, ← e₂]
140	    group
141	  choose β hβ using key
142	  -- Step 2: the coboundary relation for `β` holds on the cover `{𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒰 j ⊓ 𝒲 z}_z`
143	  -- of `𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒰 j`, hence everywhere by separation.
144	  refine ⟨β, fun i j ↦ ?_⟩
145	  refine unitsRestrict_eq_of_locally_eq
146	    (W := fun z ↦ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒲.opens z) (fun z ↦ inf_le_left)
147	    (fun w hw ↦ Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨w, hw, 𝒲.mem_opens w⟩) _ _ (fun z ↦ ?_)
148	  have e₁ := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict
149	    (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right :
150	      𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒲.opens z ≤ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒲.opens z)) (hβ i z)
151	  have e₂ := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict
152	    (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right :
153	      𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒲.opens z ≤ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒲.opens z)) (hβ j z)
154	  have e₃ := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict
155	    (inf_le_inf le_rfl (h z) :
156	      𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒲.opens z ≤ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens z))
157	    (unitsEvInf_trans γ i j z)
158	  simp only [map_mul, map_inv, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e₁ e₂ e₃ ⊢
159	  rw [e₁, e₂, ← e₃]
160	  group

162	/-- **Refinement injectivity in degree one**: for pointed covers `𝒲 ≤ 𝒰` of a scheme,
163	restriction of unit Čech `H¹` classes along the refinement is injective. -/
164	theorem unitsRes_injective {𝒰 𝒲 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) :
165	    Function.Injective (unitsRes (X := X) h) := by
166	  refine (injective_iff_map_eq_one (unitsRes h)).mpr fun a ha ↦ ?_
167	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
168	  rw [show (1 : X.unitsH1 𝒲) = OneCocycle.class 1 from rfl] at ha
169	  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ :=
170	    (OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mp ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp ha)
171	  -- restate the coboundary data through the `Γ`-typed interface
172	  have hα' : ∀ z z',
173	      X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens z ⊓ 𝒲.opens z' ≤ 𝒲.opens z) (α z)
174	          * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (h z) (h z')) (unitsEvInf γ z z')
175	        = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (α z') := by
176	    intro z z'
177	    have h1 := hα z z'
178	    rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul] at h1
179	    rw [← res_unitsEvInf h γ z z']
180	    exact h1
181	  obtain ⟨β, hβ⟩ := exists_glued_coboundary h γ α hα'
182	  rw [show (1 : X.unitsH1 𝒰) = OneCocycle.class 1 from rfl]
183	  refine (OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mpr
184	    ((OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mpr ⟨β, fun i j ↦ ?_⟩)
185	  rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul]
186	  exact hβ i j

212	    rw [← CechPic.mk_mul_mk, ← CechPic.mk_inv, hab, mul_inv_cancel]

9	/-!
10	# The relative Picard functor of a curve
11	
12	For a scheme `C` over a field `k` (an object of `Over (Spec k)`) this file defines the
13	relative Picard functor of Grothendieck–Kleiman:
14	$$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T) \;=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \times_k T)\,/\,
15	  \operatorname{Pic}(T),$$
16	line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T` modulo classes pulled back from the test object `T`
17	along the second projection. The quotient — never the absolute `Pic(C ⊗ T)`, which is
18	not even a separated presheaf in any useful sense — is the functor that étale
19	sheafification and the representability theorem consume.
20	
21	Products are the cartesian-monoidal product of `Over (Spec k)` (chosen pullbacks of
22	schemes): `C ⊗ T`, projection `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`, matching the vocabulary
23	of the challenge statement file.
24	
25	## Main declarations
26	
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase C T`: the subgroup of `(C ⊗ T).left.CechPic` of classes
28	  pulled back from `T` along the second projection.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic C T`: the relative Picard group, the quotient by
30	  `picFromBase C T`, a `CommGroup`; `relPicMk` is the projection, with
31	  `relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff` the exact coset relation (a genuine range condition, no
32	  choice, no `Nonempty (≅)`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMap C g`: restriction along `g : T' ⟶ T`, descended from
34	  pullback of Čech classes along `C ◁ g`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicFunctor C`: the relative Picard functor
36	  `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
37	-/
38

44	open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)

52	/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
53	along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
54	def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
55	  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range
56	
57	lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
58	    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
59	  Iff.rfl
60	
61	/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
62	modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
63	def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
64	  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T
65	
66	noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
67	  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)
68	
69	/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
70	noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
71	    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
72	  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)

74	lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
75	    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
76	  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)

78	/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
79	relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
80	lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
82	    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
83	  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem

88	    motive x :=
89	  QuotientGroup.induction_on x mk

94	from `T'`: the well-definedness of `relPicMap` on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
95	lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :
96	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C T').comap (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) := by

99	  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)

105	`C ◁ g` and descend to the quotients. -/
106	noncomputable def relPicMap (g : T' ⟶ T) : relPic C T →* relPic C T' :=
107	  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C T')
108	    (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) (picFromBase_le_comap C g)

124	  induction x using relPic.ind with
125	  | mk L =>
126	    rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk]
127	    refine congrArg (relPicMk C T'') ?_
128	    rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,

131	/-- The relative Picard functor `T ↦ Pic(C ⊗ T)/Pic(T)` of Grothendieck–Kleiman, as a
132	presheaf of commutative groups on `Over (Spec k)`. -/
133	noncomputable def relPicFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
134	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop)

136	  map_id T := by

138	    exact relPicMap_id C x
139	  map_comp g h := by
140	    ext x
141	    exact relPicMap_comp C g.unop h.unop x

146	  rfl
